[
  {
    "id": "DS-001",
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "rule",
    "file": "src/js/gameController.js",
    "line": 88,
    "claim": "When a player overshoots tile 100, the model does not commit the position, but the view is still told to animate a move, causing desynchronization and false turn advancement.",
    "failure_scenario": "A player on tile 99 rolls a 6, which overshoots 100. The controller leaves target_pos as current_pos, but the view's onStateChange is called and tries to animate the token from 99 to 99. The view's animateTokenMove sees previousPosition === newPosition and resolves immediately, but the autoRoll proceeds. The model has not advanced the turn in the processTurn, so the active player remains the same, leading to a continuous loop where the player repeatedly rolls and never moves.",
    "suggested_fix": "In the view's animateTokenMove or onStateChange, detect when currentPositions[i] === previousPositions[i] and skip the animation, but still call autoRoll; however, the model must explicitly call advanceTurn() when an overshoot occurs to ensure the turn passes. Alternatively, in processTurn, when moved is false due to overshoot, call this.advanceTurn() before viewing.",
    "how_to_verify": "Simulate a player on tile 99 rolling a 6. After the roll, the active player should advance to the next player and the token should remain on tile 99. The game should not stall or loop."
  },
  {
    "id": "DS-002",
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "race",
    "file": "src/js/gameView.js",
    "line": 573,
    "claim": "The view animates based on currentPositions captured before previousPositions is updated, but it also uses this.previousPositions in animateTokenMove, creating a race condition when multiple animations overlap.",
    "failure_scenario": "In a rapid sequence, onStateChange is called, currentPositions is read, and animationPromises are created. Before the promises resolve, another onStateChange is triggered by an extra roll or capture. The second call updates this.previousPositions with the first set of currentPositions. When the first animation's _animateStepByStep uses this.previousPositions, it may use the updated positions, causing incorrect paths or interrupted animations. For instance, a player's token could jump to the wrong tile.",
    "suggested_fix": "Pass the specific previous and current positions as arguments to animateTokenMove instead of relying on this.previousPositions. Update this.previousPositions immediately after reading it for each animation, and ensure animations can be cancelled or superseded gracefully.",
    "how_to_verify": "Add stress tests with rapid consecutive rolls and captures. Observe token paths and ensure they always end at the model's final positions without visual glitches or console errors."
  },
  {
    "id": "DS-003",
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "rule",
    "file": "src/js/gameView.js",
    "line": 688,
    "claim": "The view's _calculateIntermediatePosition replicates controller logic and can produce an intermediate position equal to the end position even when the controller performed a ladder or snake jump, causing the view to skip the correct jump animation and incorrectly place the token.",
    "failure_scenario": "A player on tile 36 rolls a 2. The controller moves to tile 38, then applies the ladder to tile 84, so model position is 84. In the view, _calculateIntermediatePosition(36, 2) returns 38. The hasJump condition checks if 38 is a ladder or snake start. It is not (since 38 is a ladder end, not start). The view then sets hasJump to false and animates directly from 36 to 84 without following the ladder path, potentially skipping intermediate tiles. This is not just a visual glitch; it can cause the token to animate incorrectly and may not reflect the actual jump.",
    "suggested_fix": "The view should not replicate intermediate calculation. Instead, the model should provide the full movement trace (initial tile, intermediate tile, final tile) in the state, or the view should use the controller's output to animate the exact path. Alternatively, in the controller's processTurn, record the intermediate position before ladder/snake application and store it in the model for the view to consume.",
    "how_to_verify": "Trigger a move that lands on a snake or ladder (e.g., from 36 roll 2 to ladder at 38). Observe the token's animation path. It should follow the SVG connector from 38 to 84, not a straight line."
  },
  {
    "id": "DS-004",
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "stall",
    "file": "src/js/gameView.js",
    "line": 851,
    "claim": "The _animateDirectMove relies on a transitionend event, but if the token's CSS transition is interrupted or the token is moved again before the transition completes, the event may never fire, causing the Promise to hang and the autoRoll to rely solely on the watchdog.",
    "failure_scenario": "A token is moved with _animateDirectMove. Before the transition ends, another onStateChange occurs (e.g., due to a capture affecting the same token). The new animation sets a new position and may remove the transitionend listener or cause a different transition. The original transitionend event might never fire for the first listener, leaving the Promise unresolved. The watchdog eventually fires, but if the new animation also hangs, the game may stall indefinitely.",
    "suggested_fix": "Add a fallback timeout to _animateDirectMove in addition to the transitionend listener. Use a single transitionend listener with a flag or use the Web Animations API for more reliable animation promises. Ensure all animation promises always resolve within a bounded time.",
    "how_to_verify": "Simulate rapid captures and moves involving the same token. Monitor the console for promises that never resolve and ensure autoRoll proceeds within the expected time (all animations complete within watchdog time)."
  },
  {
    "id": "DS-005",
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "stall",
    "file": "src/js/gameView.js",
    "line": 756,
    "claim": "In _animateStepByStep, the requestAnimationFrame loop for jumping may fail to resolve if the tab is backgrounded or if requestAnimationFrame is throttled, relying only on the watchdog to proceed.",
    "failure_scenario": "During a long-running autonomous game, the browser tab becomes inactive, throttling requestAnimationFrame. The jump animation loop stops progressing. The Promise never resolves, and the autoRoll is not called. The watchdog eventually fires and calls autoRoll, but the animation may be incomplete, leaving the token in a wrong position. Over time, repeated backgrounding could desynchronize the view from the model.",
    "suggested_fix": "Use a fallback timeout for the jump animation as well, or use a promise-based animation that resolves regardless of frame scheduling (e.g., setInterval with check). Ensure all animation promises resolve within the watchdog timeout.",
    "how_to_verify": "Run the game and periodically switch browser tabs or minimize during ladder/snake animations. Observe if tokens become stuck or the animation freezes."
  },
  {
    "id": "DS-006",
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "stall",
    "file": "src/js/gameView.js",
    "line": 534,
    "claim": "The game over restart timeout is not cleared when resetGame is called from elsewhere, potentially causing a duplicate autoRoll and race condition.",
    "failure_scenario": "After a game win, handleGameOver sets a 10-second timeout to restart. Before the timeout fires, the user (or a test) calls controller.resetGame() manually. The view.onReset() calls clearTimeouts(), which clears gameOverTimeout. However, if the reset happens after the timeout already fired but before the autoRoll call, a new game may start and then the old timeout's callback still runs, calling autoRoll again and potentially causing a second roll for the same turn.",
    "suggested_fix": "In handleGameOver, use a flag or store the restart timeout and always clear it in onReset. Ensure that after reset, the game over sequence is not re-entrant. Add a guard in autoRoll to check if the game is in the expected state before rolling.",
    "how_to_verify": "Add a test that triggers a win and immediately calls controller.resetGame() before 10 seconds. Observe if two autoRoll calls occur, leading to double moves or turn skipping."
  }
]
